The [[1900 Summer Olympics]], now officially known as the Games of the II Olympiad,<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 2024 |title=The Games of the Olympiad Paris 1900 and 1924 |url=https://stillmed.olympics.com/media/Documents/Olympic-Games/Paris-2024/2024-Factsheet-Paris-1900-and-1924.pdf |access-date=11 January 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref> were an international [[multi-sport event]] held in [[Paris]], France, from May 14 to October 28, 1900, as part of the [[Exposition Universelle (1900)|1900 World's Fair]].<ref name=":4">{{cite book |author=Mallon, Bill |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=inAwCgAAQBAJ |title=The 1900 Olympic Games: Results for All Competitors in All Events, with Commentary |publisher=[[McFarland & Company]] |year=2009 |isbn=9780786440641 |pages=11 |access-date=15 November 2021}}</ref> A total of 1,226 athletes representing 26 nations participated. The games featured 95 events in 19 sports.<ref name="IOC Paris 1900">{{cite web |title=Paris 1900 Summer Olympics – Athletes, Medals & Results |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/paris-1900 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220921224309/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/paris-1900 |archive-date=21 September 2022 |access-date=1 January 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=1900 Paris Olympics |url=https://sirc.ca/knowledge-nuggets/1900-paris-olympics/ |access-date=2025-01-11 |website=The Sport Information Resource Centre |language=en}}</ref> [[Archery at the 1900 Summer Olympics|Archery]], [[Basque pelota at the 1900 Summer Olympics|Basque pelota]], [[Cricket at the 1900 Summer Olympics|cricket]], [[Croquet at the 1900 Summer Olympics|croquet]], [[Equestrian events at the 1900 Summer Olympics|equestrian jumping]], [[Football at the 1900 Summer Olympics|football]], [[Golf at the 1900 Summer Olympics|golf]], [[Polo at the 1900 Summer Olympics|polo]], [[Rugby union at the 1900 Summer Olympics|rugby union]], [[Rowing at the 1900 Summer Olympics|rowing]], [[Sailing at the 1900 Summer Olympics|sailing]], [[Tug of war at the 1900 Summer Olympics|tug of war]], and [[Water polo at the 1900 Summer Olympics|water Polo]] were contested for the first time at these Games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 January 2025 |title=New sports take a bow |url=https://olympics.com/ioc/news/new-sports-take-a-bow |access-date=11 January 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref> Women competed in the Olympics for the first time during the 1900 games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Women at the Olympics |url=http://www.laici.va/content/laici/en/sezioni/donna/notizie/le-donne-alle-olimpiadi.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180923120430/http://www.laici.va/content/laici/en/sezioni/donna/notizie/le-donne-alle-olimpiadi.html |archive-date=23 September 2018 |access-date=31 July 2017 |website=Pontifical Council for the Laity}}</ref> Athletes representing 19 nations received at least one medal. France won the most of every type of medal, while the United States won the second-most of every type of medal.<ref name="oylmpedia_1900table" /> Spain,<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Medallas y Resultados – Comité Olímpico Español (COE) |url=https://www.coe.es/medallas-y-resultados/ |access-date=11 January 2025 |website=Comité Olímpico Español |language=es}}</ref> Cuba,<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=Cuba - Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/cuba |access-date=11 January 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref> the Netherlands,<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |title=Netherlands - Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/netherlands |access-date=11 January 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref> Italy,<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |title=Italy - Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/italy |access-date=11 January 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref> and Belgium<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |title=Belgium - Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/belgium |access-date=11 January 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref> all won their nation's first Olympic gold medals. Belgium,<ref name=":9" /> Italy,<ref name=":8" /> Netherlands,<ref name=":7" /> Cuba,<ref name=":6" /> Spain,<ref name=":5" /> Norway,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Norway - Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/norway |access-date=11 January 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref> India,<ref>{{Cite web |title=India - Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/india |access-date=11 January 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref> Bohemia,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Olympedia – Bohemia (BOH) |url=https://www.olympedia.org/countries/BOH |access-date=2025-01-11 |website=www.olympedia.org}}</ref> and Sweden<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sweden - Profile |url=https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/profile/sweden |access-date=11 January 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref> all won their nation's first Olympic medals of any kind.

In the early Olympic Games, several team events were contested by athletes from multiple nations.<ref>{{cite web |title=1896 - Summer Olympics I (Athens, Greece) |url=https://www.tsn.ca/olympics/feature/?fid=9337 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080618213512/http://www.tsn.ca/olympics/feature/?fid=9337 |archive-date=18 June 2008 |access-date=6 May 2008 |website=[[The Sports Network|TSN]] |publisher=}}</ref> During the 1900 games, athletes participating in mixed teams won medals in [[Football at the 1900 Summer Olympics|football]], [[Polo at the 1900 Summer Olympics|polo]], [[Rowing at the 1900 Summer Olympics|rowing]], [[Tennis at the 1900 Summer Olympics|tennis]], and [[Tug of war at the 1900 Summer Olympics|tug of war]].<ref name="IOC Paris 1900" />
[[File:Olympic_medals_Paris_1900.jpg|thumb|Gilt silver, [[silver]], and [[bronze]] medals for the 1900 Olympic Games in the Olympic Museum collection|alt=Three rectangular Olympic medals shown in a display case]]
The 1900 Olympics is unique in being the only Olympic Games to feature rectangular medals, which were designed by {{sortname|Frédérique|Vernon}}.<ref name="1900MedalDesign">{{cite web |title=Olympic Games Paris 1900 — Medal Design |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/paris-1900/medal-design |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221217235932/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/paris-1900/medal-design |archive-date=17 December 2022 |access-date=12 August 2021 |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref> [[gilt-silver|Gilt silver]] medals were awarded for first place in [[Shooting at the 1900 Summer Olympics|shooting]], [[Life saving at the 1900 Summer Olympics|lifesaving]], [[Motor racing at the 1900 Summer Olympics|motor racing]], and [[Gymnastics at the 1900 Summer Olympics|gymnastics]],<ref name=":2">{{cite book |last1=Greensfelder |first1=Jim |title=Olympic Medals: A Reference Guide |last2=Vorontsov |first2=Oleg |last3=Lally |first3=Jim |publisher=[[GVL Enterprises]] |year=1998 |pages=9–10}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite web |title=Olympic Summer Games Medals from Athens 1896 to Tokyo 2020 |url=https://stillmed.olympic.org/media/Document%20Library/OlympicOrg/Factsheets-Reference-Documents/Games/Records-and-Medals/Reference-document-OG-Medals.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200903041318/https://stillmed.olympic.org/media/Document%20Library/OlympicOrg/Factsheets-Reference-Documents/Games/Records-and-Medals/Reference-document-OG-Medals.pdf |archive-date=3 September 2020 |access-date=13 August 2021 |website=[[Olympic Studies Centre]]}}</ref> while second place [[silver]] medals were awarded in [[Shooting at the 1900 Summer Olympics|shooting]], [[Rowing at the 1900 Summer Olympics|rowing]], [[Sailing at the 1900 Summer Olympics|sailing]], [[Tennis at the 1900 Summer Olympics|tennis]], [[Gymnastics at the 1900 Summer Olympics|gymnastics]], [[Fencing at the 1900 Summer Olympics|fencing]], [[Equestrian events at the 1900 Summer Olympics|equestrian]], and [[Athletics at the 1900 Summer Olympics|athletics]].<ref name=":2" /> Third place [[bronze]] medals were awarded in [[Gymnastics at the 1900 Summer Olympics|gymnastics]], [[Fire fighting at the 1900 Summer Olympics|firefighting]], and [[Shooting at the 1900 Summer Olympics|shooting]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> However, in many sports, medals were not awarded, with most of the listed prizes being cups and other similar trophies.<ref name=":4" /> The [[International Olympic Committee]] has retrospectively assigned gold, silver, and bronze medals to competitors who earned first, second, and third-place finishes in order to bring early Olympics in line with current awards.<ref name=":4" /> [[Alvin Kraenzlein]] won four gold medals at the 1900 Summer Olympics, the most of any competing athlete.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Paris 1900 Olympic Athletes - Biographies, Medals & More |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/paris-1900/athletes |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240911072053/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/paris-1900/athletes |archive-date=11 September 2024 |access-date=2 January 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref>

== Awards ==
Prizes worth a total of 953,448 francs were awarded to the athletes across the competitions.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Mérillon |first=Daniel |url=https://digital.la84.org/digital/collection/p17103coll8/id/6404 |title=Rapports : Concours Internationaux d'exercices physiques et de sports |publisher=[[IN Group]] |location=Paris |pages=56 |language=fr}}</ref> Various cash prizes and art objects were awarded to the athletes.<ref name=":4" /> In addition, medals and plaques were distributed, including the sports plaque designed by Frédéric de Vernon, available in [[gilt-silver|gilt silver]], silver, or bronze. Produced by [[Monnaie de Paris]], the medal features two sides.<ref name=":1" /> On the front, a winged goddess holds laurel branches high above her head, with Paris and the grand monuments of the Universal Exhibition visible in the background. On the reverse, a victorious athlete stands proudly on a podium, raising a laurel branch in his right hand. Behind him, a stadium and the Acropolis of Athens serve as a reminder of the deep connection between ancient and modern Olympic traditions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Paris 1900 - The Medals |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/paris-1900/medal-design |access-date=7 January 2025 |website=International Olympic Committee}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Drevon |first=André |title=Les Jeux olympiques oubliés: Paris 1900 |publisher=[[CNRS]] |year=2000 |isbn=9782271058386 |location=Paris |pages=32 |language=fr}}</ref>

==Medal count==
[[File:Tug of war.jpg|thumb|200px|A mixed team made up of athletes from Sweden and Denmark beat the French team to win gold in the [[tug of war at the 1900 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Paris 1900 tug of war men Results |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/paris-1900/results/tug-of-war/tug-of-war-men |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007150454/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/paris-1900/results/tug-of-war/tug-of-war-men |archive-date=7 October 2024 |access-date=January 2, 2025 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]]}}</ref>|alt=A game of tug of war in the centre with a large crowd on the left.]]

The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |date=11 August 2024 |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |access-date=12 August 2024 |work=[[The Independent]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |date=18 August 2008 |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |access-date=25 July 2024 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |date=10 August 2024 |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=11 August 2024 |access-date=11 August 2024 |work=[[Diario AS]] |language=en-us}}</ref>

== Changes in medal standings ==
===Reallocation of Olympic medals to club affiliation===
====IOC attribution policy====
From the [[1896 Summer Olympics|1896]] to [[1904 Summer Olympics|1904]] Olympic Games, athletes were not always entered by [[nationality]]. The concept of national teams selected by [[National Olympic Committees]] (NOCs) did not yet exist at these Games; most competitors participated as individuals or represented their [[Sports club|sporting clubs]],<ref name="national_teams">{{cite journal |last=Mallon |first=Bill |title=United States of America (2nd International Olympic Games in Athens 1906 The Participating Countries) |journal=Journal of Olympic History |volume=14 |issue=3 |date=December 2006 |page=84 |publisher=International Society of Olympic Historians |url=https://isoh.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/136.pdf |quote=Prior to 1906, most competitors went to the Olympic Games primarily as individuals, with no national teams selected, and that was certainly the case with the United States "teams" at the 1896, 1900, and 1904.}}</ref> particularly in [[Team sport|team events]]. In such cases, participation and medals could be attributed to the country of the club rather than the athlete's nationality.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/static/faq |title=Olympedia – FAQ Nationality |work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref> Consequently, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) has applied an inconsistent approach for attributing participation and medals from the 1896–1904 Olympic Games over time, alternating between the athlete's nationality and the national affiliation of the club they represented.

*'''Team events''': Until 2024, the IOC classified all teams composed of athletes from different countries in the early [[Modern Olympic Games]] as [[Mixed teams at the Olympics|mixed teams]] ([[List of IOC country codes|IOC code]] ''ZZX''), regardless of whether they represented an established club. Since 2024, teams representing a club have been attributed to the club's country, even if they included foreign athletes. Only ad hoc teams formed solely for the Olympic Games are now classified as mixed teams.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/athens-1896/results/tennis/doubles-men|title=Athens 1896 doubles men Results - Olympic tennis|website=Olympics|access-date=2024-09-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240903184515/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/athens-1896/results/tennis/doubles-men|archive-date=2024-09-03}}</ref><ref name="Medal">{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/countries/MIX|title=Mixed team at the Olympics|work=[[Olympedia]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=2 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240502013100/http://www.olympedia.org/countries/MIX|url-status=live}}</ref>
*'''Individual events''': From 2021 to 2024, the IOC attributed medals in individual events according to the athlete's nationality, even when the athlete represented a foreign club. Since 2024, participation and medals have instead been attributed according to the national affiliation of the club represented by the athlete, largely restoring the attribution policy that had been applied for these Games prior to 2021.
<div style="visibility: hidden">&nbsp;</div>

A total of 21 medals from the 1900 Olympic Games, 8 in individual and 13 in team events, have been reallocated by the IOC since 2024.

== Notes ==
{{notelist|colwidth=1|group=upper-alpha}}
{{notelist-num|refs=
{{efn-num|name=fn1|[[George Orton]] was [[Canada at the Olympics|Canada]]'s first Olympic medalist and champion, although this wasn't immediately recognized. As the concept of national teams selected by NOCs did not yet exist at the 1900 Olympic Games, athletes were generally identified by the clubs or institutions they represented.<ref name="national_teams" /> Orton competed for the [[University of Pennsylvania]] and was consequently initially assumed to be [[Americans|American]], although he always considered himself a proud [[Canadians|Canadian]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/66202 |title=Olympedia - George Orton |work=Olympedia |access-date=22 December 2020}}</ref>}}

{{efn-num|name=fn2|[[Michel Théato]] represented a French club at the Olympics, so it had always been assumed that Théato was [[French people|French]]. Athletics historian Alain Bouillé, however, discovered that he was born in [[Luxembourg]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/68519 |title=Olympedia - Michel Théato |work=Olympedia |access-date=22 December 2020}}</ref>}}

{{efn-num|name=fn3|[[Frederick Lane]]'s nationality at the 1900 Paris Olympics is disputed. He was an [[Australians|Australian national]] although represented the [[Swim England|Amateur Swimming Association of Great Britain]] and also swam for a British club, the Blackpool Swimming Club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/45233 |title=Olympedia – Fred Lane |work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>}}

{{efn-num|name=fn4|[[Lloyd Hildebrand]]'s win in [[Cycling at the 1900 Summer Olympics – Men's 25 kilometres|cycling]] was originally assigned to Great Britain, but in 2024 it was reassigned to France by the [[International Olympic Committee]]. The IOC stated that this happened because he "was born and brought up in France, and competed for a French club before and after Paris 1900".<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2024-06-13 |title=1900 Olympics cycling medal reassigned from Great Britain to France |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/c722m1r60p2o |access-date=13 June 2024 |website=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/14746|title=Olympedia – Lloyd Hildebrand|work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>}}

{{efn-num|name=fn5|At the time of the 1900 Olympic golf event, [[Pauline Whittier]] was a US citizen but was living in [[Switzerland]] and playing her golf at the St. Moritz Golf Club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/18210 |title=Olympedia – Pauline Whittier |work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref> [[Abbie Pratt]] was also a US national in 1900 but she entered the Olympic golf tournament playing out of the Dinard Golf Club in France.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/920042 |title=Olympedia – Abbie Pratt |work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>}}

{{efn-num|name=fn6|The team race was essentially a club contest, with the [[Racing Club de France]] taking on a team from the [[Amateur Athletic Association]] (AAA) of Great Britain. Australian sprinter [[Stan Rowley]] competed for the AAA, allowing the association to field a team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/56088 |title=Olympedia – 5,000 metres, Team, Men|work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>}}

{{efn-num|name=fn7|At the 1900 Polo event, [[Foxhunters Hurlingham]] (GBR), BLO Polo Club Rugby (GBR), and Bagatelle Polo Club de Paris (FRA) won the medals in polo. All three podium teams were composed of players of mixed nationalities, reflecting the flexible team rules of the 1900 Games.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/30900 |title=Olympedia – Polo, Men |work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>}}

{{efn-num|name=fn8|An "[[unknown French boy]]" is recorded to have participated as the [[coxswain (rowing)|coxswain]] for the gold-winning. [[Mixed team at the 1900 Summer Olympics|mixed team]] (which was the [[Netherlands at the 1900 Summer Olympics|Dutch team]] prior to his joining) in the [[Rowing at the 1900 Summer Olympics – Men's coxed pair|men's coxed pair rowing]] competition.<br>Believed to possibly be the youngest Olympic medalist in history, the identity of the boy remains to this day unknown. Despite being referred to as the "unknown French boy" in Olympic archives, his nationality is not known with certainty.<ref name="olympedia_rowing1900">{{cite web |url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/157510 | title=Olympedia – Coxed Pairs, Men |publisher=Olympedia |access-date=2026-07-25}}</ref>}}

{{efn-num|name=fn9|Only three teams participated in the inaugural rugby event at the Olympics and only two games were contested. [[France national rugby union team|France]], represented by [[Union des Sociétés Françaises de Sports Athlétiques|Union des Sociétés Françaises]], played both [[Germany national rugby union team|Germany]] ([[SC 1880 Frankfurt|FC 1880 Frankfurt]])<ref>[http://www.rugby-verband.de/cms/index.php?id=75 Die Gründerjahre des deutschen Rugbysports] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071025044353/http://www.rugby-verband.de/cms/index.php?id=75 |date=25 October 2007 }} {{in lang|de}} DRV website – Foundation years, accessed: 25 February 2010</ref> and [[Great Britain at the 1900 Summer Olympics#Rugby|Great Britain]] ([[Moseley Wanderers]]),<ref name="Rugby at the Olympics">{{cite web |url = http://www.rugbyfootballhistory.com/olympics.htm |title = Rugby at the Olympics |publisher=Rugby Football History |author=Rugby Football History |access-date= 4 April 2008}}</ref> the French winning both matches.
The IOC classified the side from France, with [[Constantin Henriquez]] being from [[Haiti]], until 2024 as a "[[Mixed teams at the Olympics|Mixed Team]]". Further, [[André Roosevelt]], an American born in France, was also on the French team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/2/sports/RGB?id=TEN |title=Olympedia – Rugby at the 1900 Summer Olympics |work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>}}

{{efn-num|name=fn10|The yacht "Ollé" of [[William Exshaw]] (GBR) was the winner of both races in the 2-3 ton class, over 19 km (one long and two short rounds). [[Helmsman]] Exshaw lived in France and had two French crew members, making it a multi-national team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/9206 |title=Olympedia – 2-3 Ton Race One, Open |work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref><ref name="exshaw_profile">{{cite web |title=William EXSHAW |work=International Olympic Committee| url=https://www.olympics.com/en/athletes/william-exshaw |access-date=February 11, 2026}}</ref>}}

{{efn-num|name=fn11|[[Victor Lindberg]], a champion swimmer in [[New Zealand]] and [[Australia]], arrived in England a month before the 1900 Summer Olympics. Selected by the [[Royal Life Saving Society UK|Royal Life Saving Society]] and granted temporary membership in the Osborne Swimming Club, he competed in water polo and played in all three of the club' matches, winning a gold medal for Great Britain.<ref name="lindberg_profile">{{cite web |title=Victor LINDBERG |work=International Olympic Committee| url=https://www.olympics.com/en/athletes/victor-lindberg |access-date=February 11, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/2/sports/WPO |title=Olympedia – Water Polo at the 1900 Summer Olympics|work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref><br/>Lindberg’s nationality is complex: he was born in [[Fiji]] to [[Swedes|Swedish]] and [[Irish people|Irish]] parents and grew up in New Zealand, while representing a British club in Paris. Following the precedent set for the Australian [[Frederick Lane]], he is classified as a New Zealander rather than British.<ref name="lindberg_profile" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/80393 |title=Olympedia – Victor Lindberg |work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>}}

{{efn-num|name=fn12| Libellule de Paris has been listed as having a player by the name of "Devenot", but Olympic historian [[Bill Mallon]] identifies this player as [[Jules Clévenot]], who also competed in swimming events at the Games.<ref name="M227">Mallon 227</ref> Their squad also included [[Bill Burgess]], a Briton who would later become the second man to swim across the [[English Channel]].<ref name="BurgessSR">{{cite web|last = Gjerde|first = Arild|author2=Jeroen Heijmans |author3=Bill Mallon |author4=Hilary Evans |title = Bill Burgess Bio, Stats, and Results|work = Olympics|publisher = Sports Reference.com|date = December 2016|url = https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/bu/bill-burgess-1.html|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200418040634/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/bu/bill-burgess-1.html|url-status = dead|archive-date = 18 April 2020|access-date = 7 December 2016}}</ref>}}

{{efn-num|name=fn13|The French team included ten British nationals, two of whom were born in France, and two Frenchmen: as such, it is considered to be a mixed team,<ref name="Lloyd 2012 t005">{{cite web | last=Lloyd | first=Owen | title=Bach hints at support for cricket to be added to Los Angeles 2028 programme | website=insidethegames.biz | date=2012-10-30 | url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1140474/thomas-bach-cricket-los-angeles-2028 | access-date=2023-10-09}}</ref> though it is currently listed by the IOC as representing France.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/21150 |title=Olympedia – Cricket 1900, Men |work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>}}

{{efn-num|name=fn14|The French team, representing the [[Racing Club de France]], included 3 players who were later part of the gold-winning [[Rugby union at the 1900 Summer Olympics|rugby team]] for France. [[Jean Collas]], [[Charles Gondouin]], and [[Émile Sarrade]] were all part of both teams,{{sfn|Mallon|2009|pp=27–8}} while it is often misreported that another of their rugby teammates, the [[Haiti]]an-born [[Constantin Henriquez]] was also on the tug of war team, but this was a case of mistaken identity due to their similar names, with [[Colombi]]an-born [[Francisco Henríquez de Zubiría]] taking part in the tug of war.<ref name="mistaken">{{cite news |url=https://frr.ro/2016/03/04/rugby-ul-revine-la-jo-i-primul-campion-olimpic-de-culoare-din-istorie-a-fost-component-al-echipei-de-rugby-a-frantei/ |title=Rugby-ul revine la jo (I): Primul campion de culoare din istorie a fost component al echipei de rugby a frantei |date=4 March 2016 |language=Romanian |publisher=[[Romanian Rugby Federation]] |access-date=30 August 2017}}</ref>}}

{{efn-num|name=fn15|At the [[1900 Summer Olympics]], an [[association football]] tournament was contested for the first time. Only two matches were held between the three club sides, and no medals were awarded. France's representatives were determined by the [[Union des Sociétés Françaises de Sports Athlétiques|USFSA]], which elected the [[Paris]]ian champion [[Club Français]].<ref name=rsssf>[https://www.rsssf.org/tableso/ol1900f.html Games of the II. Olympiad - Football Tournament] by Søren Elbech and Karel Stokkermans on the [[RSSSF]]</ref> For Belgium, after [[K.F.C. Rhodienne-De Hoek|Racing Club de Bruxelles]] declined to participate, a student selection with players from the [[Free University of Brussels (1834–1969)|Université libre de Bruxelles]] was sent by the Federation.<ref>[http://en.espn.co.uk/olympic-sports/sport/story/162086.html Great Britain's first home Olympic football adventure] by Jon Carter, ESPN, 26 June 2012</ref><ref name=brown>[https://medium.com/@paulbrownUK/before-the-world-cup-who-were-footballs-earliest-world-champions-8aebac11429a Before the World Cup: Who were football’s earliest world champions?] by Paul Brown on Medium Sports, 6 June 2018</ref> The team was reinforced with a few non-students. English club [[Upton Park F.C.]] represented [[United Kingdom|Great Britain]].<ref name=rsssf/><ref name=brown/><br/> The IOC originally credited Great Britain, France and a "Mixed Team" with gold, silver and bronze medals, respectively, as part of its attempt to reconcile early Olympic Games with the modern award scheme. The Belgian team included one British and one [[Dutch people|Dutch]] player. In 2024 the bronze medal was reallocated to Belgium.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/2/sports/FBL |title=Olympedia – Football at the 1900 Summer Olympics |work=Olympedia |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>}}
}}
